My experience getting a motorbike license in Thailand

Documents required:
•	Passport
•	Residence certificate
•	Medical certificate
•	Copy of passport
•	Copy of entry stamp

You need to come on Monday, Wednesday, or Friday around 7:20–7:30 AM, take a queue number, and wait for your turn. When it’s your turn, the lady at the counter will check your documents and send you to wait in the classroom.

Then you’ll take the physical test, which includes:
•	Identifying whether the light appears on the left or right
•	Choosing the correct color (red, yellow, or green)
•	Gas/stop reaction test
•	Aligning two sticks to the same level

After that, you’ll watch 3 hours of traffic rules videos, then have a lunch break from 12:00 to 13:00, followed by one more hour of video. Then you’ll take the theory test on a computer (phones must be placed in lockers, and you can’t use it for translation, but you can ask for clarification if needed).

If you pass the theory test, you’ll take the practical test the next day at 10:00 AM. It includes:
•	Riding onto the track, using the left turn signal, and stopping before the stop line
•	The slalom test
•	Riding along a narrow line on a small slope

If you already have some riding experience, it’s quite easy. You get two attempts.
The hardest part for me was the narrow line, but don’t worry - you can always retake the test on another day.

Once you pass, you go to pay the fee, check that your name and details are correct, take a quick photo, and get your license within a few minutes.

In total, the whole process takes about 2 days.
Good luck!

After four unsuccessful attempts to get a motorcycle license from the DLT on Koh Samui, I have to give up.
But for anyone who wants to try their luck, here's a list of the required documents (in real) WITH the deadlines that must be met, which can only be found out in person. I'm simply fascinated how the same authority can come up with something different every time. It speaks for itself...
This way, at least getting admitted to the test is no longer a lottery:

• Original passport
• Signed copy of the ID page + entry stamp (MUST BE VALID FOR AT LEAST 15 DAYS)
• Copy of the current visa type (DTV, Non etc.)
• ORIGINAL certificate of residence (VALID FOR 30 DAYS AND TAKES 7 DAYS TO PROCESS)
• Medical certificate (VALID FOR 30 DAYS)

Tips:

• First pick up your certificate of residence BEFORE you do the medical certificate, otherwise you'll loose one week of vadility of your residence certificate.

•It's worth memorizing the theory questions online as best as you can, as the translation in the test is very poor and/or sometimes nonexistent.

•If you do not have an appointment (as they are booked up months in advance), be there by ~7:20a.m. at the latest to get a number.  (Mon, Wed, Fri)

• If you do not pass the theory the first time, you can try again one time immediately after at the same day.

Anyway, I hope this helps the people after me. Wish you the best of luck!

On 5-8-2025 I went to DLT Koh Samui for renewal car and motorbike license. I arrived as a 'walk-in' at 09.20 am and everything was done at 11.00 am. Quick, easy and smoothly.

Documents I provided:
-2x copy of passport personal info page and visa page.
-2x health certificate. (1x original, 1x copy).
-2x copy yellow house book and pink ID card. (with the yellow house book there's no need for a certificate of residence).
-Original passport, yellow house book, pink ID card and old driving licences.
-760 thb total for car (505 thb) and motorbike (255 thb) license.

-I made the online e-Learn test a few days before, I got the QR code, but they weren't interested in this.
-Tip: If you go a few days after your expiring date you get automatic 6 years instead of 5 years. I'm good now untill July 2031.
Great service, no worries.! 🙏🏼👍🏼

I was there on Friday at 7 AM.
For the driving license test(Motorbike), you have to go to the 2nd floor.
I didn't have an appointment.
Around 7:30 AM, the first staff members arrived.
They told me I needed an appointment and a QR code.(DLT Smart Queue App)

I said I didn't have one and that I was from Koh Phangan.
Because of that, I was told to wait until 8 AM, if there were any spots left, I could take the test today.
And that’s exactly how it went.
I had all the documents.
Copies of:
* Visa
* Passport
* Yellow Book and Pink Card
* Medical Certificate (Samui Home Clinic, 100 THB)
That was it.
Then I was sent to Room 1, where you wait to be called.
After that, you have to do 3 different tests.
But no vision test regarding distance.
After that, you have to watch 5 hours of video material, with a 1-hour lunch break.
Then the test on the PC begins.
You have to hand in your mobile phones.
If you pass it successfully (45/50)...
...you can take the practical test on the next working day.
Everyone speaks English; if necessary, you can communicate using Google Translate.
Everyone was super nice, great service.

PS: If you fail the test, you can retake it on the next day.

I passed my Category A driver's license here in two days, having prepared all the necessary documents in advance. It's important to note that Monday, Wednesday, and Friday are the days when they accept your motorcycle documents, while other days, I assume, are for a car.

On the first day, I watched five hours of lectures and took a test in English, which the DLT training website was a great help in preparing for.

The questions in the actual exam are different from the preparatory tests you can find, but the logic remains the same. Thanks to completing numerous practice exams, I passed the official exam 46 out of 50 on my first try. You need to score at least 45.

The organization was excellent, with minimal delays. The pleasant staff members were helpful and literally held my hand, explaining everything clearly.

I took the practical part of the exam at 10:00 AM on the second day, riding my bike. This is convenient. If you fail the theory test on the first day, you need to come back at 9:00 AM and try again.

The hardest part is the theoretical exam; if you pass it and ride a bike well, you won't have any problems with the practical test.

The Samui Transport Office definitely needs improvement in terms of service. You can hardly get any useful information over the phone, meaning you really have to go there in person every time. I've been there four times now, which is why I'm happy to share this information and these pictures. Driving tests are always on Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays; be there by 7:30 a.m. to get in right away. First, you'll do some physical tests (an interesting experience), and then there are several videos about the rules, signs, etc., until about noon. There's an hour's lunch break, and then it continues from 1:00 p.m. to 2:30 p.m. Afterward, there's the theory test with 50 questions, of which only 5 can be answered incorrectly. The following day, you can either retake the written test in the morning if you don't pass, and the practical driving test starts at 2:00 p.m. You have to take the test twice for both car and motorcycle licenses. There are also several websites to help you prepare for the test. The official Thai websites are only in Thai, but there are excellent English alternatives.
